component.name: Canto
component.summary: Spotify, local music, and OpenSubsonic player with synced lyrics

description.p: Canto is a GTK4 music player for the Linux desktop that puts your library, synced lyrics and listening flow front and center across Spotify, local music folders, and OpenSubsonic / Navidrome servers.

p.em: Note: Spotify streaming requires a Spotify Premium account; local folders and OpenSubsonic / Navidrome work without a Spotify account.

ul.li: Multiple music sources: Spotify (built-in audio, Soloist, or Connect), local music folders (FLAC, MP3, OGG, WAV with embedded covers), and OpenSubsonic / Navidrome servers
Synced lyrics from LRCLIB or Genius in the side panel or full screen, with word-by-word highlight, timing nudge, translation, and a 1-button Lyrics Sync Studio
Colors that follow your desktop theme (including Omarchy, matugen, pywal, wallust, and native GNOME/KDE palettes) or the album cover accent
Now Playing panel with a clickable fullscreen cover lightbox, lyrics preview, Next in Queue, song credits, and play counts from Last.fm
Your Library as a list or cover grid, with pinned items, a collapsed covers-only sidebar, in-page track filtering and quick sorting
Queue support on local and Spotify Connect devices, drag reordering, saving the queue as a playlist, and instant Recently Played history
Command palette (Ctrl+K) with instant local library search, themes, devices, sleep timer, and track radio
Scrobbling to Last.fm and ListenBrainz plus an optional JSON visual bridge for external bars and desktop widgets
Gapless playback with smooth equal-power crossfade (up to 12 s), a 10-band equalizer, stereo pan, mono, and pitch shift
Media keys (MPRIS), keyboard shortcuts, a compact mini player with seek bar and synced lyric strip, and touch gestures

description.p: Canto is a fork of Riff by Diego Augusto and contributors, itself descended from Spot by Alexandre Trendel.
